name: Observation of neutrino-like interactions without muon or electron in the Gargamelle neutrino experiment

published.note: Both papers (pp. 121 and 138) appeared in the same issue; the Crossref record dates Physics Letters B 46 to 1973-09.
published.quote: On 3 September 1973 the Gargamelle collaboration published two papers in the same issue of Physics Letters

summary.plain: In 1973 the Gargamelle collaboration reported neutrino collisions in which no muon or electron came out, only hadrons, and one event of a neutrino knocking an electron forward. CERN calls this the first direct evidence of the weak neutral current, which the theory unifying the electromagnetic and weak forces required.
summary.technical: Hasert et al. (Gargamelle), Phys. Lett. B 46 (1973) 138 (hadronic events without muon or electron) and 121 (a single antineutrino-electron scattering event), published together on 3 September 1973 after a CERN seminar on 19 July 1973. The collaboration's own title says 'Observation'; CERN's account calls it the first direct evidence of the weak neutral current.

title: Observation of neutrino-like interactions without muon or electron in the Gargamelle neutrino experiment

why_it_matters.quote: a process predicted in the mid-1960s independently by Sheldon Glashow, Abdus Salam and Steven Weinberg – that required the existence of a neutral particle to carry the weak fundamental force
why_it_matters.value: The Glashow-Salam-Weinberg theory had predicted the weak neutral current in the mid-1960s, a process that required a neutral particle to carry the weak force.
